advice.text: Measure as administrator: 3.9% of used space is unexplained.
Nothing to do: macOS frees purgeable space when it needs it.
Restarting gives back 8.6 GB of swap (it leaves the macOS line in Settings) and 1.0 GB of deleted files apps still hold (it leaves System Data). Save open work first. Swap comes back with use.
Apple Intelligence models; macOS manages them. Do not delete the folder.
Run brew cleanup --dry-run to see what it would remove. Without --dry-run it also removes old versions of installed formulae. Ask the user before running.
Empty the Trash.
Move to the Trash in Finder; apps recreate them. Space returns when the Trash is emptied.
Run xcrun simctl delete unavailable; manage the rest in Xcode > Devices and Simulators. Ask the user before running.
Delete in Finder; the next build recompiles everything.
Quit the Claude app first; this is its virtual machine.
Snapshot from another app (backup or cloning); manage it in the app that created it.
Do not delete while iCloud is syncing; usually leave it.
Anomaly: Preferences should hold kilobytes; look for the owning app.
System voices. Remove voices in System Settings > Accessibility > Spoken Content; do not delete inside AssetsV2.
Xcode documentation and Metal tools. See Xcode > Settings > Components; do not delete inside AssetsV2.
Simulator runtimes downloaded by macOS. See them with xcrun simctl runtime list; remove them in Xcode > Settings > Components. Ask the user before running.
A macOS update was downloaded. Install it or wait in System Settings > General > Software Update; macOS removes it after installing.
The Spotlight index is large. Do not delete it by hand; see System Settings > Spotlight.
There is data written to the Data volume itself, in a regular folder inside /Volumes, where there should only be mount points. It is not the disk or the share: open it in Finder and check what it is.
Do not touch: it belongs to the system and is not junk.
Do not delete: this is iCloud Drive and it would disappear from every device. Use Optimize Mac Storage.

The last backup recorded by Time Machine is from 30/09 at 21:15, and it has tried again 6 times since then without recording another. Local Time Machine snapshots hold 60.0 GB. If space runs low, macOS may delete them; then the next backup takes longer. See the destination in System Settings > Time Machine. Ask the user before running.

chronod (widgets) holds deleted copies of the LaunchServices database: 3.9 GB by the lsof logical size. The allocated size is not readable in that system folder, so it is not in the sum. Logging out or restarting gives the space back; save open work first.
